headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[Death toll reaches 1,104]] as five more die in 24 hours
headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,104 as five more die in 24 hours
summary: Bangladesh is facing an unprecedented measles crisis, with the death toll surpassing 1,100 and the country ranking first globally in infections.
details: The measles death toll in Bangladesh has reached 1,104, with five children dying in the last 24 hours. This is the highest number of deaths and infections the country has ever recorded for this disease.
According to WHO data, Bangladesh had the highest number of measles or measles-symptom cases globally between December last year and May this year, with 42,174 patients.
Health experts and public health specialists, including Dr. Mushtaq Hossain, have termed this crisis a result of 'state negligence,' citing gaps in vaccination campaigns and medical care.

Reports indicate that approximately 4 million children were missed during mass vaccination drives. Experts suggest that negligence during the previous interim government's tenure allowed the disease to resurface.
The human cost is devastating, with families in remote areas like Bandarban losing multiple children in a short span. In one instance, two brothers aged four and seven died within days of each other.
The total number of patients showing measles symptoms has surged to 190,510, and confirmed cases have reached 21,392, bringing the total patient count to 211,902.
This surge is a stark contrast to previous years; for example, in 2025, there were only 132 patients, and in 2024, there were 247 cases.

headline_marked: Human trafficking ring busted: [[Mastermind arrested in Banani]] after women's torture claims
headline: Human trafficking ring busted: Mastermind arrested in Banani after women's torture claims
summary: Two Bangladeshi women escaped from Egypt, revealing horrific torture, including cigarette burns, after being lured with promises of legal migration to Italy.
details: Special Response Battalion (SRB) arrested Mohammad Arzu Rahman (47) in Banani, Dhaka, as a key leader of an international human trafficking ring.
The arrest followed video evidence sent to the National Security Intelligence (NSI) by two women who had been trafficked to Egypt under the promise of legal migration to Italy.
The victims reported being held captive for over a year, with their passports and phones confiscated to prevent escape.
One woman detailed horrific physical and mental abuse, including being burned with cigarettes and beaten for refusing to engage in immoral acts.
The traffickers allegedly recorded videos of the torture to blackmail the victims, threatening to leak the footage on social media to shame their families.
Another victim claimed the ring took approximately 7 lakh BDT and USD 3,000 from her, while another was charged 11 lakh BDT plus USD 3,000.
The women eventually escaped one night when the house was empty, though they had to leave behind their passports and phones.
SRB reports that several other Bangladeshi women remain trapped in Egypt, and the investigation continues to rescue them.
